title: MAPWaters Act of 2025
official_title: An Act to provide for the standardization, consolidation, and publication of data relating to public outdoor recreational use of Federal waterways among Federal land and water management agencies, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Became Public Law 119-62 on December 26, 2025. Passed the House on January 21, 2025 and the Senate on December 16, 2025.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended

summary: Requires federal land and water agencies to create and publish standardized digital maps showing where the public can boat, fish, and access federal waterways, and what restrictions apply.
brief: Requires federal agencies to standardize and publish digital maps of public access and restrictions on federal waterways.

top_lines.headline: Digital Waterway Maps
subs: Agencies must publish online maps of waterway access and restrictions
Covers boating, fishing, and navigation rules
Five-year deadline to digitize and publish

items.main: Names the Act the “Modernizing Access to our Public Waters Act of 2025” (the “MAPWaters Act of 2025”).
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

items.main: Defines key terms used throughout the Act: Federal fishing restriction, Federal land or water management agency, Federal waterway, Federal waterway restriction, Secretaries, and State.
items.detail: Definitions apply throughout. "Secretaries" means the Secretary of Agriculture (acting through the Chief of the Forest Service) and the Secretary of the Interior; "Federal land or water management agency" covers the Bureau of Reclamation, National Park Service, Bureau of Land Management, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, and Forest Service.

items.main: Requires federal agencies to adopt common data standards for waterway recreation data within 30 months.
items.detail: The Secretaries of Agriculture (Forest Service) and the Interior, coordinating with the Federal Geographic Data Committee, must jointly develop interagency standards so federal databases on public recreational access to federal waterways and federal fishing restrictions are compatible and interoperable.

items.main: Requires agencies to digitize and publish online maps of waterway restrictions, access, and fishing rules within five years.
items.detail: Within five years, the Bureau of Reclamation, National Park Service, Bureau of Land Management, Fish and Wildlife Service, and Forest Service must publish geographic data on waterway open/closed status, seasonal closures, motorized and anchoring restrictions, allowed watercraft, boat ramps and fishing access sites, and federal fishing restrictions (closures, no-take zones, and gear, bait, and catch-and-release rules). Data must be updated at least twice a year (in real time for fishing restrictions), with a public comment process. The Act does not change the definition of navigable waters or federal and state fishing jurisdiction.

items.main: Lets the Secretaries partner with non-Federal, private, nonprofit, and Tribal entities, and the U.S. Geological Survey, to carry out the Act.
items.detail: Authorizes coordination with State and Tribal natural resource agencies, technology and geospatial data companies, and data-science experts, plus third-party agreements. Data must be developed under applicable Federal, State, and Tribal laws with a notice to that effect, and existing efforts (the Modernizing Access to Our Public Land Act and section 103 of division DD of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023) should be reused where practicable.

items.main: Requires the Secretaries to report progress to named House and Senate committees within 1 year and annually through March 30, 2034.
items.detail: Reports go to the House Committees on Natural Resources, Energy and Commerce, and Agriculture, and the Senate Committees on Energy and Natural Resources and on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.

items.main: States the Act does not change the definition of "navigable waters," State or Federal authority over navigable waters or fisheries, or the current accessibility of waters for hunting, fishing, or recreation.
items.detail: Rule-of-construction/savings provision — preserves existing law; no independent substantive effect.

gaps: The bill requires publishing access and restriction data but does not change any actual access rules or restrictions.
It sets a five-year publication deadline but does not provide dedicated funding for the mapping work.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Moore
featured_quotes.text: This legislation builds upon the success of my MAPLand Act, enacted in 2022, and MAP Army Corps language included in last year's Water Resources Development Act to ensure Americans can quickly see the public resources around them and spend more time recreating on the land and water they love.

added: Federal agencies must standardize and publish digital maps of public access and restrictions on federal waterways (new 16 U.S.C. 6871 et seq.)
